transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-09
Start: 17:00 PDT
Duration: 1h 2m
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Host), Alex Chen, Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Sophie Park, ~140 others (virtual)

---
Summary: Quick review of Q1 metrics, Dedicated and Private launches, SLAs and compliance, hiring updates, and Q&A.

[00:00] Maya Thompson: okay hey everyone, good afternoon and welcome to April all hands, uh thanks for joining. We'll kick off with Q1 highlights, then product updates and then q and a. please hold questions till the end, there's a slack thread.

[00:18] Alex Chen: hi all, quick note on customer momentum — we closed three Dedicated deals this quarter, two mid market and one enterprise. pipeline is healthy, there's still a lot of interest in private deployment for regulated customers.

[00:34] Maya Thompson: yeah and on revenue we beat the commit we expected, um not massive overperformance but steady growth. retention is up 3 points y/y which is great. Sophie you wanna add?

[00:48] Sophie Park: yeah retention improvements came from the CSM-led evals and the onboarding templates we shipped, those self-serve guides reduce time-to-first-inference. small caveat on account health: a couple of finance teams flagged cost predictability as a question, we're following up.

[01:10] Liam O'Connor: engineering note: latency P50 and P95 are both better after the batcher refactor, we're seeing average per-token CPU time drop about 12 to 15 percent on the sample workloads, though some long-context workloads still spike. Priya is driving a focused perf sprint next two weeks.

[01:36] Priya Singh: yeah the KV cache and smarter kernel selection landed in canary and it's promising; we still need more telemetry to tune sequence-length heuristics. also, small callout — some model names got garbled in the public bench doc, we'll fix that before publishing.

[02:00] Maya Thompson: product roadmap — quick bullets: 1) Dedicated general availability for reserved pools, 2) Private beta for VPC-managed control plane, 3) Redwood Optimize features — batch tuning recommendations and quality monitoring. Alex?

[02:20] Alex Chen: on the go-to-market side we'll be shipping a Dedicated playbook for AEs with pricing examples and SLO language. also pushing a benchmark spreadsheet — the sales motion requires clear numbers: throughput, latency, and unit costs.

[02:40] Audience Member 1: question for product — how do fallbacks between hosted and dedicated work? is it automatic?

[02:52] Priya Singh: good question. currently we have policy-driven routing; automatic fallback is supported if you opt in but it's off by default for customers that need strict data isolation. we'll be making the policies more granular so you can set region/cost/latency preference per route. forgiveness, the term we used earlier was, uh, the routing daemon handles compatibility checks, when model variants are available it can route to quantized variants as fallback.

[03:28] Maya Thompson: security and compliance update — Sophie?

[03:32] Sophie Park: SOC 2 re-cert passed two controls, the ISO audit is in flight, and we've got a prioritized POA for the remaining items. encryption at rest with KMS is live for Dedicated and Private, and we're adding HSM options for high-security customers. also working on longer retention of audit logs for enterprise add-on.

[03:58] Alex Chen: note to sales — we'll centralize the security FAQ in the sales drive, don't link to the old doc. there was some confusion around data residency language.

[04:12] Liam O'Connor: ops update: autoscaling policies now support soft and hard limits which helps burst handling without exploding costs; we've seen fewer overprovisioning incidents in staging. next steps are improving the prediction model for scaling decisions, we have an A/B experiment planned.

[04:36] Maya Thompson: hiring — headcount plan for Q2 is 22 new roles across infra, product, and sales. prioritize infra and SEs. goal is to reduce time-to-response for onboarding tickets and to accelerate the Dedicated ramp.

[04:54] Alex Chen: a few customer stories — Kestrel Financial ran a pilot on Dedicated and reported 35% cost savings vs their on-prem setup and improved latency for bursty inference. internal note: we'll ask Kestrel for a reference case, legal is on it.

[05:18] Audience Member 2: any updates on the public API pricing changes?

[05:24] Maya Thompson: no immediate price changes; we're experimenting with package discounts for committed Dedicated customers, and Optimize features will have tiered pricing. final details will come through finance and product next week.

[05:38] Priya Singh: technical note — we've improved quantized model throughput but there's a small trade-off in hallucination risk for certain tasks; the quality monitoring in Optimize will flag regressions and allow rollbacks. that's why we'll tie evals to every rollout.

[06:02] Q&A rapid fire — collected via chat and voice, recorder hiccup around 06:40 mark caused slight drop in audio for a minute. transcript may have small gaps.

[06:18] Audience Member 3: are we expanding regions to APAC?

[06:24] Maya Thompson: yes APAC expansion is Q3 priority, partner conversations are in flight; Dedicated regional availability is gated on partner infra and compliance reviews.

[06:38] Alex Chen: can we talk about ramp plan for Dedicated customers — onboarding checklist is being updated to include network diagrams, KMS setup, and egress policies, that should shorten integrations.

[06:54] Sophie Park: we'll be running office hours for customers on Dedicated onboarding starting next week; signups will be in the customer portal.

[07:06] Liam O'Connor: engineering ask to product — we need a stable API contract for model variants to avoid repeated client changes; we'll freeze minor ergonomics for a short window while ramping Dedicated.

[07:28] Priya Singh: also a note on benchmarks: some of the public numbers confused quantization settings; when we publish the benchmark spreadsheet we'll include exact config snippets and model hashes so it's reproducible.

[07:46] Maya Thompson: wrap-up — big thanks to the infra and SE teams for the hard work on Dedicated and to CSMs for retention wins. next week we'll circulate the town-hall recording and the Q&A doc. action items will be posted on the all-hands slack channel.

[08:06] Alex Chen: final note — sales folks please wait for the dedicated playbook before promising SLOs to customers, we want standard language so legal and finance can sign off.

[08:18] Audience (multiple): thanks / applause / emoji flood in chat

[08:26] Maya Thompson: meeting adjourned, thanks everyone.

---
